in strong fields (gamma < 1) one-photon annihilations are possible, and their intensity is large enough to be accessible to experiment.

a theoretical study of the radiation spectrum emitted by an e-e+ pair plasma created from vacuum by two laser beams.

The main takeaway from our work is that

in the domain of large electric fields E >> E_c, where the effective mass model is valid, the intensity of the photon annihilation radiation is proportional to the fourth power of the field intensity E^4.
the one-photon channel of annihilation is the most important one in the effective mass model, and the corresponding radiation intensity exceeds that from the other channels by orders of magnitude.
the one-photon process can be used to study the dynamics of the e-e+ plasma in strong laser fields, in particular, to estimate the plasma density and temperature.
